samples.summary: Stub `gh` call log is not one-line-per-invocation, so `calls` entries can be body text rather than commands
samples.evidence:
The stub does `appendFileSync(GH_STUB_LOG, joined + "
")` where `joined = argv.join(" ")`. mark-ready invokes `gh pr comment 7 --body <multi-line handoff>` (mark-ready.mjs:261, body built at :242-256 with `.join("
")`), so a single invocation writes ~14 lines into the log. `run()` then does `readFileSync(logPath).split("
").filter(Boolean)`, so `calls` contains hand-off prose lines as if they were separate `gh` invocations. Today no body line happens to start with `pr ready`, `pr comment` or `api -X PUT`, so `promoted()`, the `doesNotMatch`/`some` assertions and `assert.deepEqual(calls, [])` still behave — but the invariant the whole suite relies on ("one log line = one gh call") is not actually held, and any future hand-off wording starting with one of those prefixes silently flips these assertions. Encode the arg vector (e.g. JSON.stringify(argv)) per line instead.

samples.summary: The exit-code pin only matches literal `process.exit(<digits>)`, so the code that actually makes the promote job succeed silently (an uncaught exception → exit 1) is not pinned
samples.evidence: `[...SOURCE.matchAll(/process\.exit\((\d+)\)/g)]` sees only literal integer exits. It cannot see `process.exitCode = N`, `process.exit(code)` with a variable, or — most importantly — an UNCAUGHT exception, which makes node exit 1. Exit 1 is the value the workflow maps to "leaving as draft; job succeeds" (agent-review-panel.yml:1399), i.e. exactly the "PR sits as a draft forever" outcome this file's header says it exists to catch. mark-ready has un-try/caught top-level work (e.g. the `computeLabelSet`/JSON paths are wrapped, but any future top-level throw would not be), so a real regression could exit 1 with this test still green. Consider also asserting the absence of `process.exitCode` writes and/or a top-level try/catch that maps unexpected throws to 2.
searchedFor: read all of mark-ready.mjs for uncaught throw sites

samples.summary: The workflow-contract test does not pin `set +e`, without which exit 1 would fail the job while all four assertions still pass
samples.evidence: The test asserts `/code=\$\?/` and the four `-eq N` branches, but the branch semantics depend entirely on `set +e` at agent-review-panel.yml:1391. Delete that one line and `run:`'s implicit `set -e`... (GitHub `bash -e`) aborts the step at line 1392 with the raw non-zero status, so exit 1 becomes a FAILED job (and exit 3's dedicated message never prints) — yet `code=$?` and every `-eq` regex in this test still match, so the suite stays green. Add an assertion that `set +e` precedes the invocation inside the same window.
searchedFor: grep set +e in the promote step

samples.summary: Every `run()` leaks a temp directory; nothing removes them
samples.evidence: `mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "mark-ready-"))` is called once per `run()` (~20 invocations across the file, several inside loops) and no `rmSync`/`after()` hook removes any of them. Each leaks the stub `gh` binary, a config and a log. Harmless per run, but it is an unbounded accumulation in developer/CI temp space and makes the suite non-hermetic on repeated local runs.

samples.summary: stdout assertions depend on console.log output surviving an immediate `process.exit`, which is not guaranteed for pipes on macOS
samples.evidence: The tests match on stdout produced immediately before `process.exit(...)` in mark-ready.mjs (e.g. :183-184 "Not promoting…" then exit 1; :188-189 then exit 0). Node's stdout is synchronous for pipes on Linux/Windows but ASYNCHRONOUS for pipes on macOS, so `process.exit` can truncate the final writes there. `spawnSync` with `encoding: "utf8"` uses pipes, so `assert.match(stdout, …)` can flake for local macOS developers even though the CI lane (ubuntu) is safe. Asserting on the exit code alone, or having the CLI use `process.exitCode` + natural exit, would remove the dependency.
